summary.intent: Fold a latent pin-leak fix for `restoreFileVersion`'s web hook into PR #494, then audit all mutative web app calls to confirm they route through the new SDK client methods rather than direct `sdk-core` publishes.
summary.outcome: Fixed `restoreFileVersion` to unpin SDK-returned `prunedCids` (not just web-computed ones), removed ~310 lines of dead upload code (`handleAddFile`/`handleAddFiles`) that bypassed `client.folderTree`, confirmed all active mutation paths route through the SDK client, and committed the combined fold-in with root typecheck and all affected tests passing.

repo: `prunedCids` has two independent sources: web-computed cap-pruning (deterministic) and SDK-returned conflict-merge pruning (only on 409). They are conceptually disjoint but must be unioned and deduped when unpinning.
`useSharedWriteOps.ts` uses `SharedWriteContext`/refs rather than `client.folderTree` by design — shared-with-me folders are a separate subsystem, not a bypass.

Active single/batch upload routes through `useDropUpload.ts:147` → `getSdkClient().uploadFiles()`. The `handleAddFile`/`handleAddFiles` methods in `useFileOperations.ts` were dead code using the old direct `sdk-core` pattern.
`useFolder.ts:39` re-exports the entire `useFileOperations` object, so verifying dead code required tracing that no consumer destructures `.addFile`/`.addFiles` from `useFolder()`.

Of 38 audited operations: 18 correctly routed through SDK client, 11 legitimately out-of-scope (device-registry, vault-settings, BYO config — separate non-folder IPNS records), 9 were bypasses (2 dead code, 5 by-design shared-folder subsystem, 2 duplicates).

code.finding: Restore hook was only unpinning web-computed `prunedCids` and discarding the SDK-returned `prunedCids` from conflict-merge — same latent pin-leak as `deleteFileVersion` but not flagged by CodeRabbit.
`handleAddFile` is dead code — calls `addFileToFolder` directly from `@cipherbox/sdk-core`, bypassing `client.folderTree`. No live consumer exists despite being re-exported via `useFolder`.
`handleAddFiles` is dead code — calls `addFilesToFolder` directly from `@cipherbox/sdk-core` (publishes IPNS at `sdk-core/src/folder/index.ts:565`), bypassing `client.folderTree`.
`restoreFileVersion` already returns `prunedCids` from the SDK; the web hook was silently discarding them before this fix.

All five shared-write operations (`uploadToSharedFolder`, `createSharedSubfolder`, `renameInSharedFolder`, `updateSharedFile`, `deleteFromSharedFolder`) use `SharedWriteContext` built from folder refs — by design, not a folderTree bypass.

workflow: A 5-agent parallel audit workflow (38 ops, 107 tool uses, ~263k tokens) was effective for mapping SDK-routing coverage across the web app surface.
Delegating a mechanical ~310-line deletion to a sub-agent with exact constraints + typecheck gate kept the main context lean without losing correctness guarantees.
Background + unsandboxed commit mode is required when the 1Password signer needs Touch ID; this should be anticipated before committing in that environment.
Verification chain: root typecheck (all package builds + web `tsc -b`) + per-package test suites before committing — typecheck alone is insufficient for catching import-removal regressions.

friction: 1Password Touch ID prompt is required for background unsandboxed commits, introducing a manual gate that can stall automated commit flows.
The audit workflow result was truncated at 20,880 chars in the task notification, requiring a separate full-file read to get the complete findings map.
The `useFolder.ts` re-export pattern obscured dead-code status of `addFile`/`addFiles` — tracing required two additional grep passes to confirm no live consumer.
open_items: Commit `bpclf138s` was running in background at session end — push to `feat/phase-47-sdk-folder-state-publish-consolidation` (PR #494) still pending confirmation.

`useSharedWriteOps.ts` shared-write paths are currently out-of-scope for `client.folderTree` integration — if shared folders are ever brought under unified state management, these five call sites need to be migrated.
Broader Phase 47 SDK folder-state publish consolidation work likely continues beyond PR #494.
